page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 24 vCPUs and 24 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits average multi-core performance but struggles with single-core workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core CPU test falls in the middle 50%. Geekbench testing shows a strong multi-core score in the top 25%, contrasted by an average single-core score. Memory performance is mixed, with PassMark memory scores in the bottom 25%, though memory bandwidth read and write tests consistently achieve average tiers. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly, reaching the top 25% of tested systems.

The shared CPU allocation model introduces potential resource contention, which explains the lower single-core performance metrics. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-thread CPU performance. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, memory-heavy data processing, caching layers, and database operations that benefit from a large memory footprint but can tolerate shared CPU resources.
